HOW TO HANDLE IT: if Jordan is run tonight, the honest line is that the toll has
been revised upward during the day and that approved sources do not agree - the BBC
still carries seven from Friday evening, Al Jazeera carries eight citing Jordan's
health ministry at 14:39 BST, and the Guardian carries nine with 40 injured at
15:24 BST. The eight figure is the only one with a named institutional attribution
in hand. Do not write a single bare number.

OTHER FACTS, ATTESTED, from the Al Jazeera piece in hand:
- THREE masked gunmen. Still unidentified and at large as of 14:39 BST.
- Location: Saint George's Greek Orthodox Church, village of Hamoud, Karak
  governorate. Attack was during a funeral service on Friday afternoon.
- Survivors said they heard an explosion just after the start of the service. Two
  attackers arrived in a vehicle and were joined by a third carrying a semi-automatic
  rifle. They entered the church and opened fire for several minutes.
- Named survivor: Nasser al-Burqan, a lawyer, told Reuters that one of the
  attackers, standing about two metres away, pointed a handgun at him and fired.
  Quote: "When everything finally quietened down, I looked out the window behind me,
  and I saw two [assailants] - one was masked, the other was not; he was carrying a
  handgun."
- King Abdullah II said those behind the attack would face the "harshest penalties"
  and offered condolences to victims' families. He has ordered a review of the
  country's security procedures for responding to terrorist attacks.
- Jordanian authorities are treating it as an act of terror. Al Jazeera notes it is
  a rare attack on a Christian place of worship in Jordan.
